transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-28
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM); Priya Singh (NexaHealth Eng Mgr), Tom Boudreaux (Platform Lead), Elena Park (Security), Jamal Ortiz (SRE)

Summary: quick weekly sync to check onboarding progress, credential handoff, staging environment readiness, and alignment on next bench/rollout playbook. A few infra blockers remain: KMS policy confirmation, VPC peering details, and a KV-cache tuning pass needed for latency-sensitive paths.

Topics: onboarding status; access and creds; security/KMS; benchmarking plan; rollout/playbook; next steps and owners

----- Transcript -----
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll run quick round the table and then dive into the staging readiness. Diego and I will cover the bench plan and KV cache notes. Samir will cover the rollout/playbook.
[00:18] Priya Singh: Hi, yeah, thanks. Quick update from our side, we gave staging team the creds yesterday, they hit an auth error so we tweaked the IAM role, should be resolved but haven't re-run the smoke tests yet.
[00:30] Tom Boudreaux: I can add, the peering request is in but our infra team needs routes - we didn't include the route table entries for the Redwood gw, so that is pending.
[00:42] Diego Alvarez: Ok noted. From Redwood side we've seen that missing routes show up as 403-ish connection failures, so that's consistent. Jamal, are you able to confirm whether the peering is accepted or still pending?
[00:55] Jamal Ortiz: It's accepted but route propagation hasn't happened. We'll need the exact CIDR ranges Redwood expects — is that in the onboarding doc?
[01:08] Maya Chen: Yes, it's in the network diagram I shared - but I'll reattach it. Diego, quick on the CIDR - send the exact /20 list in the chat.
[01:20] Diego Alvarez: I'll paste it after the call. Also, on the KV-cache: we noticed with short chat-like prompts the cache hit rate is low with default settings, which increases token compute. We can push suggested prefix caching and smaller batch windows to improve p95 latency.
[01:40] Priya Singh: That would help, our latency SLO is 150ms p95 for lookups so anything over that is a problem. Are those changes disruptive?
[01:50] Diego Alvarez: Non-disruptive, config-only. But for the best results we recommend a quick benchmark so we can tune in prod-like traffic. We'll run two benchmarks: short prompt heavy and long-context heavy.
[02:05] Priya Singh: OK.
[02:10] Elena Park: On security - KMS integration: we need to confirm key policies and whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys with automated rotation. Also, audit logs need to tie back into our SIEM, is there an out-of-the-box connector?
[02:28] Maya Chen: Good questions. We support customer-managed KMS in Private and Dedicated deployments; for Hosted we have an integration pattern. Rotation is supported via KMS; I'll include our security packet that has the exact policy examples and rotation cadence. Audit logs can be exported and we have a compressed event schema - Diego, can you add the logging export note to the packet?
[02:50] Diego Alvarez: Yep, I'll add an example CloudTrail/Flow log config and a sample ingestion mapping for common SIEMs.
[03:05] Tom Boudreaux: Also curious about RBAC - can we map our existing groups to token roles so we don't have to onboard new users manually?
[03:16] Samir Patel: We have SSO + SCIM support; mapping to our route-level roles is standard. We'll send the mapping doc and a quick checklist for mapping groups to routes and rate limits.
[03:30] Priya Singh: Great. On the bench plan: what traffic profile do you need from our staging? We want to minimize noise for other teams.
[03:40] Diego Alvarez: Two profiles: 1) 10k short requests over 10 minutes (quick-turn chat) to stress throughput and latency, 2) 1k long-context requests across 2GB sequences to test memory/kv behavior. We can stage them off-hours; expected load will be similar to what you see in production ramp.
[04:00] Priya Singh: We can do the short test next Tuesday 03:00 UTC and the long test Thursday 01:00 UTC. We'll confirm in calendar.
[04:10] Maya Chen: Perfect.
[04:20] Jamal Ortiz: Quick note on fallback: if we hit capacity limits, can Redwood automatically fall back to a smaller model or queue requests? We need this in the runbook.
[04:32] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we support fallback policies — model variants and capacity-tier routing. We'll include example policies in the rollout playbook, including expected cost tradeoffs.
[04:45] Priya Singh: Cost transparency is big for execs; can you show example unit cost for 2B quantized vs 7B quantized and hosted vs dedicated?
[04:56] Maya Chen: We'll include a clear cost comparison spreadsheet. I'll add a committed vs burst scenario so you can see monthly burn estimates.
[05:08] Elena Park: Anything about data residency? Some PII in logs — we need assurance the logs retained in staging won't cross regions.
[05:20] Samir Patel: We have region pinning for logs and retention policies. For the pilot we can restrict logs to eu-west-1 if needed. We'll note that in the security packet.
[05:35] Priya Singh: Ok, moving to rollout/playbook. Samir, can you walk us through the handoff steps?
[05:42] Samir Patel: Sure, handoff is 6 steps: 1) credentials + VPC confirmation, 2) smoke bench + KV tuning, 3) security sign-off (KMS + logs), 4) canary with 1% traffic and automatic rollback, 5) ramp to 25% with monitoring checks, 6) full rollout. Each step has a checklist and gating criteria.
[06:05] Tom Boudreaux: For canary we need explicit rollback thresholds (errors > 1.5% for 5 mins) and latency regressions (p95 > 200ms for 10 mins). Can you make those thresholds configurable?
[06:18] Samir Patel: Yes, thresholds are editable in the playbook; we can set your thresholds as defaults and add alerts to your pager channels.
[06:30] Priya Singh: We also expect a readout after canary with numbers on cost delta - if quantization or batch windows increase per-token cost.
[06:40] Diego Alvarez: We'll include a per-route cost delta report that shows tokens/second and estimated $/hour with current config vs tuned config.
[06:52] Maya Chen: Quick note — for the canary, we recommend a dedicated small pool to avoid noisy neighbor effects. That will be in the reserved-capacity proposal.
[07:05] Priya Singh: Understood.
[07:10] [09:12] 
[07:15] Diego Alvarez: small aside—there was a transcription note, sorry—um—on batching windows: smaller windows reduce latency but decrease throughput efficiency. For your SLO we think 50ms window is the sweet spot with prefix caching.
[07:34] Priya Singh: Could we do dynamic windows based on traffic?
[07:38] Diego Alvarez: Yes, adaptive batching is possible; we can ship a config that increases batch size at higher QPS. We'll show the sim numbers.
[07:50] Tom Boudreaux: On the KMS front, question — do you require us to provide HSM-backed keys for pilot or is software KMS acceptable?
[07:59] Elena Park: (overlap) Our security standard prefers HSM for keys in prod but pilot can use software KMS if it's locked down.
[08:08] Maya Chen: We can accept software KMS for pilot; for Dedicated/Private we'll support HSM. We'll denote those stages in the doc.
[08:20] Priya Singh: Great. Anything else?
[08:24] Jamal Ortiz: I wanted to flag an SRE concern: request tracing must propagate across our internal services - is there a tracing header Redwood can accept?
[08:35] Diego Alvarez: We support B3 and W3C trace context headers — we'll add examples.
[08:44] Jamal Ortiz: Perfect.
[08:50] Maya Chen: Ok let's align on dates: Diego will send tuning doc by 09-30, Maya will send pricing and network diagram by 09-30, Samir will attach the rollout playbook and checklist by 10-01. Customer to confirm bench windows and provision peering by 10-02.
[09:10] Priya Singh: We'll confirm the bench slot and provide the peering routes by 10-02.
[09:18] Maya Chen: Any blockers on your side for the upcoming bench?
[09:22] Tom Boudreaux: Just peering route table entries and KMS decision for pilot — otherwise we're good.
[09:30] Elena Park: We'll aim to get the KMS policy to you by 10-04.
[09:35] Maya Chen: Great. Quick recap of action items and owners, then we'll wrap.
[09:40] [45:30] 
[09:42] Closing notes: Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the next 24–48 hours with the docs. If anything urgent ping me directly.
[09:50] Priya Singh: Thanks all.

Referenced artifacts/links: network-diagram.pdf (attached), security-packet-sample.docx (to be sent), reserved-capacity-spreadsheet.xlsx (to be sent), bench-schedule-calendar-invite (TBD)

End of transcript.
